title: Elide earlier random-key shuffles before final Fisher-Yates
question: Can earlier adjacent auto/uniform shuffles be removed while preserving every explicit resident requirement?
summary: Use narrow mixed elision in ordinary builds, preserving final-method execution and every earlier explicit Fisher-Yates obligation.

workloads: Native root/retained, wide, upstream-fusion bypass and downstream exact assignment; three alternating pairs.
WASI root/retained and integrated downstream/composed complete jobs.

validation.summary: Independent final-permutation proof, original-index/domain and logical/physical observations, explicit resident-only failures, parent isolation, immutable prepared Analysis ownership and output/cleanup verification.

limitations: Native root effect is small; upstream fusion is an unchanged bypass, not a gain.
Wide-row fitting path increases RSS/reservations; identical shared-pressure success domains are not promised.
Small warm WSL2/bundled-Chromium development samples do not establish native Windows/macOS, other browsers, scale or tails.
Working reservations are not RSS; Analysis temporary counters precede publication; final committed-head CI is separate.
An inherited parser-owned shrink replacement-overlap gap remains in unchanged baseline producers; new mixed-prefix intake retains actual capacity.
Private archive readback used the existing OAuth principal; no separate scoped-reader or public publication claim.
exclusions: Warmups, failed attempts and source-mismatched/quarantined WASM output are excluded from measured comparisons.
Derived summaries and repeated verification records are not additional observations; cells/runtimes are not pooled.
reopen_when: Reopen broader mixed-method rules only with explicit-method/failure obligations and a separate measured eligible path.
